query: How active is the 2026 US tornado season and what is the forecast/outlook for early July 2026 severe weather? Current ENSO state (La Nina/El Nino) for summer 2026 and any Climate Prediction Center outlook for July 2026 severe convective weather in northern Plains and Midwest.
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings:

**Most important correction:** The premise of "La Niña for summer 2026" is outdated. The **actual summer 2026 ENSO state is El Niño (strengthening)** — CPC issued an El Niño Advisory around June 11, 2026, with the latest Niño-3.4 index at **+1.2 °C** (IRI showed +1.55 °C in June). CPC gives 97% odds El Niño persists into early spring 2027 and ~81% odds of a "very strong" event by Oct–Dec. An earlier late-2025 CPC forecast had projected La Niña→neutral through summer, but the ocean warmed faster than expected.

**2026 tornado season:** Above-average but front-loaded and erratic — March 204 (3rd most active on record), a quiet May (119, suppressed by the ENSO transition weakening the jet), then a hyperactive June (315, most active since 2010). ~1,100–1,164 preliminary reports through early July; Illinois set a state record.

**Early July 2026 severe weather (northern Plains/Midwest):** Active but not outbreak-level. Peak was the **July 2 SPC Enhanced Risk** (Dakotas/MN/WI) with 75+ mph winds and large hail (wind/hail-dominant, only 2% tornado prob), plus Slight Risks July 7 and July 9. Wisconsin hit 39 tornadoes by July 20.

**CPC July outlook:** Leaned hotter (East/central US) and drier (parts of Plains). By late July, CPC's Hazards Outlook shifted focus to **rapid-onset drought and heat** in the Dakotas/Corn Belt rather than severe convection. Note: CPC doesn't issue a formal monthly "severe convective" outlook — that's SPC's domain.

I flagged data-quality caveats where AI-generated aggregator sites gave inconsistent figures.

key_facts: Summer 2026 ENSO state is El Nino (strengthening), NOT La Nina; CPC issued an El Nino Advisory ~June 11, 2026, with latest weekly Nino-3.4 index at +1.2C.
CPC gives 97% chance El Nino persists through early spring 2027 and ~81% chance of a 'very strong' El Nino in Oct-Dec 2026, potentially among the strongest on record.
The La Nina-to-El Nino transition suppressed May 2026 severe weather (only 119 confirmed tornadoes vs ~265-275 average) via a weaker subtropical jet.
2026 tornado season is above-average and front-loaded: March 204 (3rd most active on record) and June 315 (most active June since 2010).
National preliminary tornado report counts cited around 1,100-1,164 through late June/July 2, 2026; Illinois set a state record and led the nation.
July 2, 2026: SPC Enhanced Risk (level 3/5) for northern Plains into Upper Midwest (Dakotas/MN/WI) with 75+ mph winds, large-to-very-large hail, 15% hail prob, 30% wind prob, 2% tornado prob.
SPC issued Slight Risks for the northern High Plains/Upper Midwest and central Plains on July 7 and July 9, 2026.
Wisconsin's 2026 tornado count reached 39 by July 20, well above its annual average.
CPC July 2026 outlook leaned hotter across the East/central US and drier across parts of the Plains; no dedicated CPC monthly severe-convective outlook exists (SPC handles convective outlooks).

CPC Hazards Outlook valid Aug 1-7 2026 (issued July 24) highlighted Rapid-Onset Drought in the Great Plains/Corn Belt (D0/D1 expansion in the Dakotas as of July 21) and extreme-heat risk, not severe convection, for the northern Plains/Midwest.
Confirmed 2026 monthly tornado totals: Jan 21, Feb 49, March 204, May 119, June 315.
2024 was near-historic with 1,796 preliminary tornadoes (2nd-most on record); 2025 had ~1,383 for context.
